title: [Audit] 🔎 Elasticsearch Data Access
description: What data was read, by whom, through which transport action — including system indices.

config.content:
### What data was read or written in Elasticsearch, and by whom

See which indices each identity uses, the kinds of requests they made, any denied requests, and every touch of system or hidden indices. Raw records: [All audit events](/app/discover#/view/cloud-audit-search-00-all-events), [Raw signal feed](/app/discover#/view/cloud-audit-search-10-raw-signal-feed).

Related indices are grouped into one family, so a data stream and its daily backing indices read as a single row. Use it to confirm that sensitive data is reached only by the people and keys you expect.

**How to use it:** choose a Project, Person (email), API key or Client IP in the controls and set the time picker. Empty denied and system-index panels usually mean all is well.

- This page counts all traffic, these dashboards’ own reads included: on a page about who reads what, those reads are the subject.
- A request counts once per index it names; shard copies and internal sub-steps are left out. Ranked tables show the top rows; the tiles count everything.
- Matrix: a blank cell means no reads, or too few to be among the 500 busiest identity–family pairs.
- System and hidden index access is expected from Kibana and platform automation; from anyone else, look closer.
- The chart legend’s totals leave out the partial bucket at the right edge, so they can run behind the tiles.

config.description: All Elasticsearch audit events in range. The line above the number compares it with the prior period of the same length.

Distinct index families named in requests. A data stream and its backing indices, or a run of dated indices, count as one family; system and hidden indices count once per area. Wildcard patterns are not counted.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL AND (elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("indices:data/read/esql/search_shards", "indices:data/read/esql/data"))) | STATS BY elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE LOCATE(elasticsearch.audit.indices, "*") == 0 AND NOT elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE "<*" | EVAL family = REPLACE(REPLACE(elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^\.ds-""", ""), """[-.]?\d{4}[.-]\d{2}[.-]\d{2}(-\d+)?$""", "") | EVAL family = REPLACE(family, """[-.]\d{8}[-.T]?\d{6}(?:[-.].*)?$""", "*") | EVAL family = CASE(LEFT(family, 1) == ".", CONCAT(REPLACE(family, """^(?:\.ds-)?(\.(?:alert-actions|[^-._]+)).*$""", "$1"), "*"), family) | STATS `Index families` = COUNT_DISTINCT(family)

config.description: Distinct Elasticsearch transport actions (cluster:*, indices:*), the same actions Top transport actions lists, all traffic.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE elasticsearch.audit.action IS NOT NULL | STATS BY elasticsearch.audit.action | WHERE NOT (elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql/*") | STATS `Distinct actions` = COUNT(*)

config.description: ES|QL queries submitted, one per query rather than per shard or sub-step. Includes the queries these dashboards run to draw themselves. The line above the number compares it with the prior period of the same length.
Requests touching system and hidden indices (.kibana*, .security*, .slo-*, .alerts-*), counted once per index named. Ordinary data-stream backing indices are not system data and are left out.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | MV_EXPAND elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE ((elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".*" AND NOT elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-*") OR elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-.*") AND (elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*") | STATS `System index access` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Authorization denials. Sustained non-zero values mean a misconfigured client or a probe. The line above the number compares it with the prior period of the same length.

config.title: Data access over time by action family
config.description: Elasticsearch requests over time by kind of action (read, write, admin…), all traffic, including these dashboards’ own reads. Each request counts once. The legend gives each kind’s total; a gap means no audited requests then.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE elasticsearch.audit.action IS NOT NULL | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY time = BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), elasticsearch.audit.action, request = elasticsearch.audit.request.name | WHERE NOT (elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql/*") AND NOT (elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/search" AND COALESCE(request, "-") == "") | EVAL family = CASE(elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read*", "read", elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/write*", "write", elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:admin*", "index admin", elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:admin/xpack/security*", "security admin", elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:admin*", "cluster admin", elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*:monitor*", "monitor", "other") | STATS events = SUM(n) BY time, family | SORT family

config.title: Who reads which index family · up to 10 identities
config.description: The busiest identities (up to 10) across the top, the index families they read down the side. Color runs teal (fewest events) to pink (most), on a log scale. A blank cell means few or no reads.

config.title: Top index families by events · 14 at most
config.description: The busiest index families across all traffic, with how many identities touched each and the busiest one. Over a quiet range this is often just the audit stream, read by the identity these dashboards run as.

data_source.query: SET unmapped_fields="nullify"; FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL AND (elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("indices:data/read/esql/search_shards", "indices:data/read/esql/data"))) | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY user.email, api_key.name, user.name, elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE LOCATE(elasticsearch.audit.indices, "*") == 0 AND NOT elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE "<*" | EVAL actor = COALESCE(user.email, api_key.name, user.name, "<anonymous>"), index = REPLACE(REPLACE(elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^\.ds-""", ""), """[-.]?\d{4}[.-]\d{2}[.-]\d{2}(-\d+)?$""", "") | EVAL index = REPLACE(index, """[-.]\d{8}[-.T]?\d{6}(?:[-.].*)?$""", "*") | EVAL index = CASE(LEFT(index, 1) == ".", CONCAT(REPLACE(index, """^(?:\.ds-)?(\.(?:alert-actions|[^-._]+)).*$""", "$1"), "*"), index) | STATS n = SUM(n) BY index, actor | EVAL k = CONCAT(TO_STRING(n + 1000000000000), actor) | STATS events = SUM(n), actors = COUNT(*), top = MAX(k) BY index | SORT events DESC, index | LIMIT 14 | EVAL busiest = SUBSTRING(top, 14) | EVAL busiest = CASE((LENGTH(busiest) == 20 AND busiest RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT busiest RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(busiest, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), busiest) | KEEP index, busiest, actors, events

config.title: Top transport actions · 13 at most
config.description: The busiest Elasticsearch actions with their request type and how many identities sent each, all traffic, including these dashboards’ own reads. Each request counts once. The Distinct actions tile counts every action, listed or not.

data_source.query: SET unmapped_fields="nullify"; FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE elasticsearch.audit.action IS NOT NULL | STATS n = COUNT(*), seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY user.email, api_key.name, user.name, elasticsearch.audit.action, request = elasticsearch.audit.request.name | WHERE NOT (elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*" OR elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql/*") AND NOT (elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/search" AND COALESCE(request, "-") == "") | EVAL actor = COALESCE(user.email, api_key.name, user.name, "<anonymous>"), request = CASE(request IS NULL OR request == "", "—", request) | STATS events = SUM(n), actors = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor), last_seen = MAX(seen) BY elasticsearch.audit.action, request | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 13

config.title: Denied requests by identity · newest 10 at most (empty = good)
config.description: Who was refused, newest first: each identity’s latest denied action and index, how many actions and indices, and its denials. A last row “N other identities” holds the rest; index “—” is a cluster-level request.

data_source.query: SET unmapped_fields="nullify"; FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE event.action == "access_denied" OR event.action == "anonymous_access_denied" | STATS events = COUNT(*), seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY user.email, api_key.name, user.name, elasticsearch.audit.action, elasticsearch.audit.indices | EVAL actor = COALESCE(user.email, api_key.name, user.name, "<anonymous>"), k = CONCAT(TO_STRING(seen), "|", COALESCE(elasticsearch.audit.action, "—"), "|", COALESCE(elasticsearch.audit.indices, "—")) | STATS events = SUM(events), last_seen = MAX(seen), latest = MAX(k), actions = VALUES(elasticsearch.audit.action), indices = VALUES(elasticsearch.audit.indices) BY actor | EVAL sk = CONCAT(TO_STRING(last_seen), "|", actor) | INLINE STATS ids = COUNT(*), recent = VALUES(sk) | EVAL cut = MV_MIN(MV_SLICE(MV_SORT(recent, "DESC"), 0, 8)) | EVAL actor = CASE(ids > 10 AND sk < cut, "~rest", actor) | STATS events = SUM(events), last_seen = MAX(last_seen), latest = MAX(latest), actions = VALUES(actions), indices = VALUES(indices), folded = COUNT(*) BY actor | EVAL actor = CASE(actor == "~rest", CONCAT(TO_STRING(folded), " other identities"), actor) | EVAL latest_action = MV_SLICE(SPLIT(latest, "|"), 1), latest_index = MV_SLICE(SPLIT(latest, "|"), 2), actions = COALESCE(MV_COUNT(actions), 0), indices = COALESCE(MV_COUNT(indices), 0) | KEEP actor, latest_action, latest_index, actions, indices, events, last_seen | SORT last_seen DESC | LIMIT 10 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: ⚠️ Who touched system and hidden indices · newest 25 at most (empty when none in range)
config.description: Who touched system and hidden indices (Kibana internals, security, alerting, SLO data), with the index groups, kinds of action and request count. Expected from Kibana and platform automation; from anyone else, a write is worth a look. Scroll for more.

data_source.query: SET unmapped_fields="nullify"; FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE elasticsearch.audit.indices IS NOT NULL | MV_EXPAND elasticsearch.audit.indices | WHERE ((elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".*" AND NOT elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-*") OR elasticsearch.audit.indices LIKE ".ds-.*") AND (elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*[*") | STATS n = COUNT(*), seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY user.email, api_key.name, user.name, elasticsearch.audit.indices, elasticsearch.audit.action | EVAL actor = COALESCE(user.email, api_key.name, user.name, "<anonymous>"), area = CONCAT(REPLACE(elasticsearch.audit.indices, """^(?:\.ds-)?(\.(?:alert-actions|[^-._]+)).*$""", "$1"), "*") | EVAL family = CASE(elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read*", "read", elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/write*", "write", elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:admin*", "index admin", elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:admin/xpack/security*", "security admin", elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:admin*", "cluster admin", elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "*:monitor*", "monitor", "other") | STATS events = SUM(n), indices = COUNT_DISTINCT(elasticsearch.audit.indices), groups = VALUES(area), kinds = VALUES(family), last_seen = MAX(seen) BY actor, api_key.name, user.name | EVAL groups = MV_CONCAT(MV_SORT(groups), ", "), kinds = MV_CONCAT(MV_SORT(kinds), ", ") | KEEP actor, api_key.name, user.name, groups, kinds, indices, events, last_seen | SORT last_seen DESC | LIMIT 25 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Raw system index requests · newest 1,000 at most (empty when none in range)
config.description: The raw requests behind the system index table above, one row per index named, newest first: one request naming ten indices is ten rows. Capped at 1,000, so it can show fewer than the tile counts.
